title: Functions
summary: Define and call functions, pass arguments, return values, and write arrow functions.

concepts.title: Functions as values and arrow functions

misconceptions.description: Believes writing a function declaration runs its body.
Believes a function call waits until the lines after it have run.
Reads the value a variable has at the end of the program for every earlier step.
Counts the first run of a line as run zero.
Believes arguments are matched to parameters in some order other than position.
Believes a parameter keeps a value from an earlier call or step instead of the current one.
Believes changing a parameter also changes the variable that was passed in.
Believes a function gives back its last computed value or its argument without a return.
Believes lines after a return still run, or that a later return can replace an earlier one.
Believes a function name without parentheses runs the function, or the reverse.

conceptCard.title: Defining a function
conceptCard.body: A function is a named block of code. Writing it only defines it. The code inside runs each time you call the function with its name and parentheses.

conceptCard.title: Parameters and arguments
conceptCard.body: A parameter is a name in the function header. An argument is the value you pass in the call. Arguments fill the parameters by position, and each call starts fresh.

conceptCard.title: Returning a value
conceptCard.body: return gives a value back to the place of the call and ends the function. A function without return gives back undefined.

lessons.title: Functions as values and arrow functions

conceptCard.title: Functions as values
conceptCard.body: A function can be stored in a const. An arrow function uses =>. Without braces its expression is returned automatically; with braces you need return.
